title: Forward generation does not ensure GNS descent: an explicit continuous counterexample
description: Generation by an observed algebra and its forward translates does not ensure descent through a general dilation's fixed expectation-GNS representation. This research note constructs a unital separable, injective, point-norm continuous C*-dilation of the two-state exponential relaxation semigroup, exactly forward-generated by C2. Its GNS image is M2, and an explicit nonzero positive kernel element leaves the kernel at every positive time. This refutes the concrete generation-only proposal in Skeide's 2009 module-approach problem. The clock/evaluation/cocycle mechanism is credited to Burgarth, Facchi and Hillier; the negative phenomenon is also a short unstated corollary of their earlier clock model. Finite-unitary and first-derivative antecedents are credited to Dive, Mintert and Burgarth and to vom Ende. No new general dilation method or literature-first priority is claimed. Stronger minimality conditions and extension after separately imposed kernel invariance remain outside the result. The verification archive preserves the original PR candidate, independent analytic audits, primary-source attribution evidence and reproducible exact checks. AI tools were used extensively in construction, writing and verification. This is an unrefereed preprint; internal AI reviews do not constitute human peer review.
